name: Civil unrest
value: France protests continue; Guinea clash deaths
summary: France held a fifth protest Saturday on 14 Nov and a strike day on 17 Nov; at least 10 killed in Guinea mining clashes
state: France saw a fifth straight Saturday of nationwide cost-of-living protests on 14 Nov, with about 106,000 marchers by the interior ministry's count and 200,000 by organisers' count; unions called a further strike day for 17 Nov and no deaths were reported (Euronews). In Guinea, the government said at least 10 people were killed in clashes in Siguiri on 12–13 Nov over a ban on artisanal gold mining (Arab News). Sustained protests and localised deadly unrest keep Watch; no deadly nationwide unrest in a major country was found as of 18 Nov.
for_you: Protests in France can disrupt transport and city centres on strike days. FCDO travel advice for France and Guinea carries current safety information.
rubric_hit: Watch: significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one (France 106,000 on 14 Nov; Guinea at least 10 killed 12–13 Nov)

sources.title: Euronews — France sees fifth consecutive Saturday of nationwide protests
Arab News — 10 killed in clashes in Guinea after artisanal mining ban

why: Mass protest and state crackdowns signal political fragility and can topple governments.
drivers: Cost of living, elections, corruption, repression, food and fuel prices.

rubric.alert: Deadly nationwide unrest or a state crackdown in a major country.
rubric.watch: Significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one.
rubric.normal: No deadly mass unrest in large countries.
